intro: A frequency sketch trades exact counts for bounded memory. Several hash rows reduce collision overcounts, and the minimum row counter estimates each queried frequency.
task: Build a compact frequency sketch from explicit hash mappings and compare collision inflation across counter rows.
requirements: update_hashes is an integer-valued (N,D) matrix and query_hashes is an integer-valued (M,D) matrix, D>0. width is an integer 1..10000 and every hash index lies in [0,width-1].
counts is a length-N vector of nonnegative integer-valued increments up to 1000000. Add each increment to the selected bucket in every sketch row.

Return dict sketch as a (D,width) integer array and estimates as a length-M integer vector taking the minimum selected counter across rows. Hashes are caller-supplied; use ordinary updates, not conservative updates.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Each update touches every depth
hints.body: Rows are separate counter arrays, even if bucket indices happen to match.

hints.title: Use the minimum estimate
hints.body: Nonnegative collisions can only add count, so the smallest row counter is the least inflated estimate.

explanation: With nonnegative increments, every queried counter includes the true frequency plus possible collision contributions. Taking the minimum cannot introduce an underestimate for a consistently hashed item.

Statistical error bounds require assumptions about the hash family and sketch dimensions. The lesson exposes supplied bucket mappings so collisions can be examined directly without claiming those probabilistic guarantees.
